differentiation.occupancy_preservation: The objective compares soft assignment distributions rather than pulling every residual toward one code. This does not guarantee balanced hard-SID occupancy: measure per-level occupancy, entropy, and Gini, and reject the arm if occupancy collapses or retrieval regresses.

vs_r8.why: Uses directed KL between full soft assignments over codebook rows, rather than contrastive classification over directed L1 code transitions.
Does not add an L1 next-item semantic prediction head or prediction target; it regularizes pairwise assignment distributions directly.
Uses directed source-to-target assignment KL for individual behaviour pairs, not symmetric JS matching of successor profiles.
Does not solve an entropic transport or quantizer assignment problem; it uses differentiable row-wise softmax assignments and a low-weight pair loss.
Does not distil a teacher into three code levels; the declared objective is defined on the supplied residuals and codebook.
Does not preserve graph diffusion distances; it uses directed observed behaviour pairs and their soft code assignments.
Uses Euclidean residual-to-codebook distances and no hyperbolic gyro-translation.
Uses no hyperbolic space or Frechet successor barycentres.
Uses no radial hierarchy or branching constraint in hyperbolic space.
Uses no graph-code Gromov-Wasserstein objective or hyperbolic graph matching.
Unlike the untouched host control, this adds a low-weight behaviour-pair objective with an explicit codebook gradient; its downstream value must be established by matched evaluation.

differentiation.vs_reference_arm: Unlike the gentle codebook-reaching geometry-transport reference arm, this mechanism directly regularizes the directed target-versus-source soft assignment distributions and tests that specific asymmetry. It does not claim an ER or downstream gain; the low activation weight and occupancy/retrieval selection criteria are intended to avoid repeating strong-assignment collapse, which must still be checked empirically.

equation: L = sum_{b: m_b=1} KL(p_t^b || p_s^b) / max(1, sum_b m_b), where p_s^b = softmax_c(-||s_b - e_c||^2 / tau) and p_t^b = softmax_c(-||t_b - e_c||^2 / tau).
expected_failure_modes: The host overwrites the encoder gradient and the auxiliary term consequently produces no effective encoder update.
The codebook gradient is zero, non-finite, or large enough to concentrate assignments into very few rows.
Soft assignment KL improves while exported hard SIDs or Stage-3 candidate recall and ranking worsen.
The directed objective is numerically unstable for sharp assignments or produces non-finite loss or gradients.
The auxiliary term is effectively inactive, yielding bit-identical model parameters and exported SIDs to the control.

forbidden_substitutions.reason: Reverses the declared KL direction and changes the mechanism's source-target asymmetry.
Blocks the required codebook gradient, so the host's surviving gradient path cannot alter exported codes.
Replacing soft assignments with hard argmin assignments changes the objective and can remove useful gradients.
Blocks a declared residual gradient target and changes the proposed end-to-end geometry update.

hypotheses: For valid directed user-item behaviour pairs, training will organize residuals and codebook rows so that target soft assignments are predictable from source soft assignments; this may preserve or improve downstream candidate retrieval.

This objective is a proposal, not evidence of downstream improvement. Select it only if a matched cold run improves Stage-3 recall@10 without reducing NDCG@10, and if hard-SID occupancy and retrieval checks show no collapse or regression.
The auxiliary term must deliver a measurable codebook gradient on the host's assembled training path; a pre-assembly gradient alone does not qualify.

revision.reason: proposed from the ledger's supported findings, not from a fixed lever list
revision.supersedes: the two families the ledger measured in issue #105

symbols.KL(p_t^b || p_s^b): Directed Kullback-Leibler divergence from target assignment distribution to source assignment distribution.
symbols.L: Auxiliary loss for directed behaviour pairs.
symbols.b: Index of a source-target behaviour pair in the batch.
symbols.e_c: Codebook row c, supplied as codebook[c].
symbols.m_b: Pair-validity mask; 1 means valid and 0 means excluded.
symbols.p_s^b: Soft code assignment distribution for the source residual, computed over all codebook rows.
symbols.p_t^b: Soft code assignment distribution for the target residual, computed over all codebook rows.
symbols.s_b: Source item residual representation for pair b, supplied as source[b].
symbols.t_b: Target item residual representation for pair b, supplied as target[b].
symbols.tau: Positive soft-assignment temperature; smaller values sharpen assignments.

tests.statement: On the declared synthetic case with at least one valid pair, the loss is finite and nonnegative.
Permuting codebook rows leaves the loss unchanged within tolerance.
For the declared non-degenerate synthetic case, exchanging source and target changes the loss beyond tolerance.
Masking every pair produces exactly zero loss and finite zero gradients.
With valid, non-degenerate pairs, gradients with respect to source, target, and codebook are finite and nonzero.
On the host's training path, the auxiliary term changes the assembled codebook gradient relative to the matched control; separately record the encoder gradient before and after host assembly.
Compare treatment and control using matched configuration and cold-run evaluation; accept only if Stage-3 recall@10 improves and NDCG@10 does not decline, with no hard-SID occupancy collapse.

title: Behaviour-directed soft code-transition KL
